description.cancellation_policy:
Change Policy:

Changes to your reservation cannot be made after printing your permit. Your permit may be printed up to seven days in advance of your arrival date.

Changes to your reservation are allowed as long as they are made at least one day in advance to your permit and prior to printing it.

Changes to the number of the campers upon arrival for your permit cannot be processed.

In order to make a change you will have to log-in to the website, www.recreation.gov, or call 1-877-444-6777. Changing the entry date or entry zone will require cancelling the original reservation (a $6 cancellation fee applies) and booking a new reservation.

Cancellation Policy:

If you cancel your reservation at least two days in advance of your reservation, you will receive a refund minus a $6.00 service fee. If you cancel less than two days in advance, there will be no refund.
description.description:
Under the stars, near the sound of the surf, waking to a chorus of song birds, camping on Fire Island within the Otis Pike Fire Island High Dune Wilderness can be a memorable experience. This backcountry camping experience is available by permit only. 

Two backcountry camping zones are available within the Otis Pike Fire Island High Dune Wilderness, the eastern and western zones. 

Access is through the western gateway to wilderness, Watch Hill or campers may hike in from the Wilderness Visitor Center in the east, adjacent to Smith Point County Park.
description.discounts:
Annual Fee Cards:

America the Beautiful Interagency Passes, including senior, access, and annual passes, do not apply to backcountry overnight camping permits.
description.driving_directions:
By ferry from Patchogue: Take the ferry to Watch Hill or Davis Park and check in at the Watch Hill Visitor Center. Hike east. The western backcountry zone begins one mile past the Watch Hill Campground. 

Watch Hill Ferry Terminal Site is located at 150 West Avenue in Patchogue, New York, 11772. 

By Car: 

From the Long Island Expressway (LIE or I-495), take Exit 61 S onto County Road 19 (Patchogue-Holbrook Road). 

From Sunrise Highway (Route 27), take Exit 52 South onto County Road 19 (Patchogue-Holbrook Road/Waverly Avenue). 

About 1 mile from Rt. 27, bear left. Cross Main Street, go over the railroad tracks, and cross Division Street. Ferry terminal parking lot is ahead on your right. 

By Train: 

Take the LIRR to Patchogue Station. 

By car from Smith Point: Take the William Floyd Parkway south to the end and check in at the Wilderness Visitor Center. Hike west. The eastern camping zone begins on the west side of Old Inlet, about 2 miles west of the visitor center.

By Car: 

From the Long Island Expressway (LIE or I-495), take Exit 68 S onto County Road 46 (William Floyd Parkway). 

From Sunrise Highway (Route 27), take Exit 58 South onto County Road 46 (William Floyd Parkway). 

Note - there is no parking available at the Wilderness Visitor Center. Please plan to be dropped off and picked up.
description.fee_policy:
A $25.00 permit fee is assessed for each permit.

An additional fee may be necessary to purchase a passenger ferry ticket to Watch Hill or Davis Park.

description.need_to_know_email:
The following rules and regulations apply to Fire Island National Seashore Permits for backcountry camping: 

Check-in is required upon arrival at the Visitor Center during hours of operation. For after hours and off-season arrivals a self check-in station is available at the Dune Station along the main dune crossing at Watch Hill or outside the entrance to the Wilderness Visitor Center or you may email your permit number and check-in date to: fiis_camping_check-in@nps.gov 

Permittee is required to have one print or digital copy of their permit upon check-in. Permit is to be retained by the permittee at all times during camping. 

Permittee must be 21+ years of age and carry valid, government issued photo ID. 

From Watch Hill, it's 1 mile to the western zone and 4 miles to the eastern zone. From the Wilderness Visitor Center, it's 2 miles to the eastern zone and 4 miles to the western zone.

Carry in drinking water and all necessary supplies, and carry out all trash. Be prepared for ticks and mosquitoes when the weather is warm. 

Open fires are prohibited; use a backcountry stove for cooking. 

Bury human waste in cat-holes dug six to eight inches deep and at least 200 feet from water. 

Camping permits only valid for the length of stay that they are issued for. 

No camping on the primary dunes or within 20 feet of the toe of the dunes. 

Campsites are not assigned, but you must select a suitable site which will not disturb vegetation, dunes, or nesting shorebirds. Your site must also be no closer than 300 feet from other campers. 

No camping within 1,000 feet of Bellport Beach. 

No camping within 200 feet of piping plover enclosures or nesting threatened and endangered species. 

No camping within symbolic fencing. 

No trenching around tent. 

No permanent camping facilities will be built. 

No vehicle access permitted for camping. 

No pets permitted March 15 through Labor Day on the beach or in the wilderness. 

If you have additional questions, email FIIS_Information@nps.gov
description.need_to_know_order:
Please be aware that you and your party will need to hike on soft sand 1 to 3 miles from Watch Hill to reach the western camping zone, and 4 to 5 miles from Watch Hill to reach the eastern camping zone. From the Wilderness Visitor Center, parties will need to hike 2 to 3 miles to reach the eastern zone and 4 to 5 miles to reach the western zone. 

This is a carry-in, carry-out area. Bring drinking water and all necessary supplies, and carry out all garbage. Water at park facilities is shut off the last Thursday in October each year.

Be prepared for ticks and mosquitoes when the weather is warm! 

Open fires are prohibited; use a backcountry stove for cooking. 

If you have additional questions, please email FIIS_Information@nps.gov
description.need_to_know_pdf:
The following rules and regulations apply to Fire Island National Seashore permits backcountry camping.

  • Check-in is required. Campers must check in upon arrival at the Visitor Center during hours of operation. A self-check-in station is available at the Dune Station along the main dune crossing for after hours and off-season arrivals. Please sign in and retain your permit during your stay.

  • Permittee is required to have one print or digital copy of their permit upon check-in. Permit is to be retained by the permittee at all times during camping.

  • Permittee must be 21 years of age or older and carry valid, government issued photo ID.

  • No open fires; camp stoves only.

  • Bury human waste in cat-holes dug six to eight inches deep and at least 300 feet from water.

  • Carry in/carry out all trash and personal items.

  • No pets permitted March 15 through Labor Day on the beach or in the wilderness.

  • Camping permits only valid for the length of stay that they are issued for.

Choosing a Campsite

  • Campsites are not assigned, but you must select a suitable site which will not disturb vegetation, dunes, or nesting shorebirds.

  • Your site must also be no closer than 300 feet from other campers.

  • No camping on the primary dunes or within 20 feet of the toe of the dunes.

  • No camping within 1,000 feet of Bellport Beach and the wilderness breach.

  • No camping within 200 feet of piping plover exclosures or nesting threatened and endangered species.

  • No camping within symbolic fencing.

  • No permanent camping facilities will be built.

  • No vehicle access permitted for camping.

  • No camping permits will be issued to hunters.

  • No trenching around tent.

Preparing for your trip

  • You and your party will need to hike on soft sand one to three miles from Watch Hill to reach the western camping zone, and four to five miles from Watch Hill to reach the eastern camping zone.

  • Carry in drinking water and all necessary supplies, and carry out all trash.

  • Open fires are prohibited; bring a backcountry stove if you plan on cooking.

  • Be prepared for ticks and mosquitoes when the weather is warm.

  • Plan for quickly changing weather conditions.

  • If you have additional questions, email FIIS_Information@nps.gov or call the Office of Interpretation at 631-687-4780.

Please note: Fire Island National Seashore does not accept walk-ins. 

The following rules and regulations apply to Fire Island National Seashore Permits for backcountry camping:  

  • Check-in is required. Campers must check in upon arrival at the Visitor Center during hours of operation. For after hours and off-season arrivals a self check-in station is available at the Dune Station along the main dune crossing at Watch Hill or outside the entrance to the Wilderness Visitor Center or you may email your permit number and check-in date to: fiis_camping_check-in@nps.gov 
  • Permittee is required to have one print or digital copy of their permit upon check-in. Permit is to be retained by the permittee at all times during camping. 
  • Permittee must be 21 years of age or older and carry valid, government issued photo ID. 
  • Camping permits only valid for the length of stay that they are issued for. 
  • No camping on the primary dunes or within 20 feet of the toe of the dunes. 
  • No open fires; camp stoves only. 
  • Bury human waste in cat-holes dug six to eight inches deep and at least 200 feet from water. 
  • Camp at least 300 feet away from other campers. 
  • No camping within 1,000 feet of Bellport Beach. 
  • No trenching around tent. 
  • No camping within 200 feet of piping plover exclosures or nesting threatened and endangered species. Learn more about piping plover monitoring and management on Fire Island. 
  • No camping within symbolic fencing. 
  • No permanent camping facilities will be built. 
  • No vehicle access permitted for camping. 
  • No camping permits will be issued to hunters. 
  • Carry in/carry out all trash and personal items. 
  • No pets permitted March 15 through Labor Day on the beach or in the wilderness.   

 

Help ensure a safe visit to Fire Island National Seashore

  • Protect yourself from the sun 
  • Watch out for poison ivy 
  • Use caution in & around the water 
  • Be aware of rip currents
  • Avoid ticks and mosquitoes 
  • Never feed or touch wildlife 
  • Keep dogs leashed 
  • Be aware of NPS alcohol policy
description.no_show_policy:
If you do not cancel and decide not to use your reservation, none of the fees will be refundable.

Please cancel your reservation if you are unable to use it as this opens space for others.
description.quota_details:
The maximum number of permitted campers in the eastern zone is 12 per night with a maximum of four campers in each site.

The maximum number of permitted campers in the western zone is 24 per night with a maximum of eight campers in each site.
description.season_information:
This permit allows the holder to camp within the Otis Pike Wilderness. 

Two backcountry camping zones are available, the eastern and western zones. There is a three-night limit for backcountry camping. 

Eastern Zone: Maximum number of campers is 12 per night with a maximum number of four campers allowed in each site. The nearest access to the Eastern Zone is on foot from the Wilderness Visitor Center, a 2 to 3 mile hike. 

Western Zone: Maximum number of campers is 24 per night with a maximum number of eight campers allowed in each site. The nearest access to the Western Zone is on foot from Watch Hill, a 1 to 3 mile hike. 

From March 15 to Labor Day, backcountry campsites may be selected on the beach in front of the eastern zone or western zone, in areas where there are no restrictions or closures. From early September through March 14, campers must select campsites behind the dunes in wilderness within either the eastern or western zone. 

Permittee must be 21 years of age or older.

payload.directions:
For Eastern Zone: Take the William Floyd Parkway South. Once across the bridge the visitor center is ahead and to the right.

For Western Zone: Off of the exit 52 from Sunrise Highway (SR27) travel south on Waverly Ave. Bear left at the traffic circle to head east and cross Main Street.

The Ferry termianl is 1/8 mile after crossing trains. A ferry to Watch Hill is required to access. Ferrys are seasonal.
